title: Driver enjoyed fast lane ; Man shot and killed by OPP no stranger to traffic cops
article: A Hammond man killed in a confrontation with OPP north of Brockville had a history of traffic-related run-ins with police, court documents show.
The province's Special Investigations Unit yesterday identified the victim in the Friday night incident as 35-year-old Phillip Jeffrey Charbonneau.
An autopsy has confirmed Charbonneau died of a gunshot wound.
Information obtained by Sun Media from a records check found Charbonneau had not made any payments on a $5,000 fine he'd been handed in October 2008 for driving while his licence was suspended.
Police pulled him over in Alfred-Plantagenet, east of Hammond, on Sept. 13 and charged him under the Highway Traffic Act.
A month later, he was convicted of the offence and handed the stiff penalty.
It wasn't Charbonneau's first traffic-related run-in with the law.
In April 2007, he was convicted of careless driving and fined $320.
A year later, in March 2008, Charbonneau was found guilty of speeding -- doing 96 km/h in an 80-km/h zone -- and fined $50.
In May 2008, he was again convicted of speeding -- this time for doing 80 km/h in a 60-km/h zone -- and fined $90.
On Friday at about 11 p.m., OPP officers shot and killed Charbonneau after he allegedly struck an officer with his pickup truck.

The OPP says two police officers suffered minor injuries in the incident, which resulted from a chase after Charbonneau allegedly bolted from a RIDE check on the Hwy. 401 off-ramp at County Rd. 29 in Brockville.
According to the SIU, the OPP's attempt to block the fleeing suspect "resulted in a collision between the truck and OPP vehicles."
Officers then "interacted" with the suspect and "at some point the truck struck an officer," the agency adds.
"Two officers discharged their firearms and the driver was struck at least once.
The male was pronounced dead at the scene," the SIU statement adds.
The SIU is appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident to contact it at 416-622-1965 or 1-800-787-8529, ext. 1965.
The SIU has two "subject officers" on the investigation, as well as eight "witness officers."
Under the law, witness officers are required to co-operate with the SIU, while subject officers have the right not to speak to investigators, said SIU spokesman Frank Phillips.
